newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks end modestly up amid IPO flood.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks end modestly up amid IPO flood.

text.p: U.S. stocks struggled to a slightly higher finish as the market digested more than a dozen initial public offerings and investors hunkered down for the upcoming spate of economic indicators.

"We had a tidal wave of IPOs. But this market seems to be in a long pause. There's a lack of conviction and we have a good deal more economic reports next week," said Marty Kearney, a trader at PTI Securities.
The Dow industrials rose four to about 5873. For the week, the Dow fell about 16 points.
Kearney noted that the Dow has climbed more than four percent so far in September, which is a positive development in what is historically the weakest month of the year. Winners

beat losers 6-5 on heavy NYSE volume of about 404 million shares. The S&P 500 rose fractionally to 696. The NYSE Composite inched up to about 366.27, topping Thursday's record 365.99. The Nasdaq Composite rose two to about 1230, drawing ever nearer to June 5's record high finish of 1249.15.
The long bond lost 8/32 to yield 6.91 percent. Treasuries fell on profit-taking after a strong run this week following the Fed's decision on Tuesday to hold interest rates steady.
Wall Street next week faces September National Association of Purchasing Management index, August new home sales, leading indicators and Friday's key September employment data.

"Stocks are straggling on fears of a slowdown in the fourth quarter. But as in the past there's the usual difficulty for the market in reaching the next plateau, in this case 6000" for the Dow, said Peggy Farley, chief executive officer of Amas Securities.
"We had a full calendar of IPOs this week with the last part of the week not showing as good a performance as they should have," she said.
"The euphoria the (IPO) market saw in the spring has dissipated, there's less confidence," Farley added.

Stocks debuting on Friday included Spanish-language TV broadcaster Univision Communications, up 8-1/2 to 31-1/2, and Swiss watch maker Tag Heuer International, which rose to 20 on the NYSE from its $19.55 a share pricing.

IPOs Cox Radio Inc surged 3-1/2 to 22. Abacus Direct, a provider of group behavioral statistics for the catalog industry, and sunglasses maker Gargoyles rallied 4-9/16 to 20-9/16. RockShox, a maker of bicycle suspension products, rose 1/4 to 15-1/4, and Lightbridge rose 1-5/8 to 11-5/8.
Among other newly public companies, temporary staffing company StaffMark rose two to 14, Nitinol Medical was up 1/4 to 11-1/4 and CellNet Data fell to 19 from its $20 pricing.

As for the overall market, "the action has been quite good. It was a very volatile week and a lot of that volatility has been constructive in helping to arrest excesses," said Eugene Peroni, chief technical analyst with Janney, Montgomery Scott. He said technology stocks may pull back after rallying recently on hopes for improving profits, short-covering and window-dressing. "They need to correct. They went a little too far too fast. I see a consolidation, not liquidation."
In special situations, Dow component GE rose 1-1/8 to 91-1/2. Goldman Sachs upgraded GE to the firm's recommended list from market outperform.

PepsiCo slumped 2-1/8 to 28-1/8 after its warnings that 1997 share earnings will fall $0.10 below Street expectations. Late on Thursday, the company said third-quarter earnings will fall from a year ago due to an estimated $360 million pre-tax charge for its international beverage business.
Providence Journal Co class A shares soared 8-1/8 to 28-7/8 and A.H. Belo lost 3-3/8 to 34-1/8. Belo agreed to buy Providence in a $1.5 billion stock and cash deal.
Signet Banking fell 5/8 to 26-3/8 after hitting a 52-week high of 29 on takeover speculation. The company said it is not for sale and was not in any merger discussions.
Whirlpool shed 1-5/8 to 50-1/2 after forecasting that third-quarter operating results will be about 35-40 percent below year-ago levels. First Boston downgraded the stock.
ValuJet fell 7/8 to 12. The Association of Flight Attendants union said it would file for a stay of the Transportation Department's decision to let the airline resume operations.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 2.07 to 1230.05.
The S&P 500 index rose 0.33 to 686.19.
(Figures official as of 1645 EDT/2045 GMT)
